title: Hired 3 marketing agencies in 2 years — all terrible. What am I doing wrong?
target_audience: Law firm owners who engaged with agency accountability content

messages.trigger: Comment, share, or like on the post
messages.template:
Hey [NAME] 👋

Saw you engaged with that post about the $57K agency disaster. Guessing you've felt that pain before?

The worst part isn't the money lost—it's wondering if *any* agency can actually move the needle for your firm.

Would be happy to share what we've learned from firms who broke the cycle. No pitch, just insights.

Interested?
messages.goal: Start conversation based on shared frustration. Build rapport. Gauge openness to discussion.

messages.trigger: Reply to message 1 (any response) or no response after 20 hours
messages.template:
Quick thought, [NAME]:

Most law firms measure marketing wrong. They track:
- Leads (should be "qualified conversations")
- Clicks (should be "consultations booked")
- Impressions (should be "signed cases")

One firm we worked with switched from tracking leads to tracking actual case value. Found out their "best performing" campaign was their worst performer.

Cost them $18K/month for 6 months before they realized.

What metric are you currently using to judge if your marketing is working?
messages.goal: Provide concrete insight. Ask diagnostic question to understand their current measurement gaps. Position expertise without selling.

messages.trigger: Reply to message 2 or no engagement from message 2 after 20 hours
messages.template:
Based on what you've shared, I think a 15-min audit could be really valuable.

We'd look at:
- How you're currently measuring ROI
- Gaps in your tracking (most firms have big ones)
- One quick fix you could implement this week

Zero obligation. Just a conversation.

Does Tuesday or Wednesday work better for a quick call?
messages.goal: Soft CTA for consultation. Lower barrier (15 min). Specific value prop. Clear next step with time options.

expected_reply_rate: 18-24% (warm engagement-based audience typically 15-25%, law firm owners tend toward higher engagement on ROI content)
